records.text: The Pendragon Cycle drove The Daily Wire into the ground financially and was an abject financial failure.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And here are the main takeaways from the article. Finally, they admit that Pendragon, the Pendragon cycle, Jeremy Boreing's pet project is what caused a significant amount of financial duress for the company. ... I want you to process that. That is... That is mania. That is Jeremy (Jeremy Boreing)'s mania. Okay. That is the single greatest contributor to the fall of the company.

And that is what happened. Pendragon, Jeremy (Jeremy Boreing)'s high school dream, drove the company into the ground financially with a project. I want to be clear that not even Disney Studios would have invested tens of millions of dollars in. That's a tremendous financial risk. He thought it was going to be a roaring success. It was an abject financial failure.

verification.notes: The available financial reporting does not show that The Pendragon Cycle drove Daily Wire into the ground. Reporting describes the project as unusually expensive and the company later had layoffs and subscriber decline, but Semafor reports that Daily Wire still produced more than 200 million dollars of 2025 revenue and 48 million dollars of adjusted EBITDA. No project-level audited result proves whether Pendragon itself earned a return.

records.text: Owens cited reporting that The Daily Wire spent $50 million on seven episodes of The Pendragon Cycle, while maintaining that the total was closer to $60 million.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: OK, they finally admitted that they spent 50 million dollars. ... On just seven episodes, that is just to understand how crazy and insane that is. They spent actually, by the way, to be clear, I've been saying the whole time, more than $50 million, closer to 60, but at least they're finally admitting that it wasn't $10 million or $7 million as it had been reported in the past.

verification.notes: Semafor reports that The Daily Wire spent 50 million dollars on The Pendragon Cycle, and The Daily Wire identifies the first season as seven episodes. The reported 50 million dollar and seven-episode components are confirmed. No reliable source was found for the additional assertion that the true total was closer to 60 million dollars.

records.text: Owens asserted that The Daily Wire spent more per episode on The Pendragon Cycle than HBO spent on the entire first season of Game of Thrones.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That means they spent more per an episode than HBO spent on the first season of Game of Thrones.

verification.notes: Semafor reports a total 50 million dollar spend for the seven-episode Pendragon production, or about 7.1 million dollars per episode. HBO reported that the full ten-episode first season of Game of Thrones cost about 60 million dollars. Therefore one Pendragon episode did not cost more than the entire first Game of Thrones season. The statement appears to confuse a per-episode comparison with an entire-season comparison.
